reader_summary.headline: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6NZ podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6NZ podcast. Today we're continuing our ongoing podcast series covering different aspects of the coronavirus pandemic. As a reminder, you can catch all past and recent content on this at A6NZ.com slash coronavirus.

key_points.text: Today's topic is on tracking networks of spread for predicting pandemics and loads, which has implications for resource allocation, getting back to work.
key_points.evidence_quote: Today's topic is on tracking networks of spread for predicting pandemics and loads, which has implications for resource allocation, getting back to work, and much more.

key_points.text: Our guest is sociologists and physician Nicholas Christakis, who directs the human nature lab, part of the Yale Institute for Network Science.
key_points.evidence_quote: Our guest is sociologists and physician Nicholas Christakis, who directs the human nature lab, part of the Yale Institute for Network Science.

key_points.text: He and his collaborators previously published work in PLOS on the H1N1 pandemic, which informed their newly released app, Hunala.
key_points.evidence_quote: He and his collaborators previously published work in PLOS on the H1N1 pandemic, which informed their newly released app, Hunala, which is an example of a privacy-preserving approach for tracking pandemics to allow not just rapid warning, but early detection.

key_points.text: Also, a quick note that we have another episode on not just tracking and predicting, but the privacy aspects of contact tracing.
key_points.evidence_quote: Also, a quick note that we have another episode on not just tracking and predicting, but the privacy aspects of contact tracing, a separate but very related topic on 16 minutes.
